subject: mlops
q: What is MLOps?
a: DevOps practices plus versioning, testing and monitoring of data and models, so ML stays reliable in production.
analogy: DevOps for a program whose behaviour also depends on data.

subject: mlops
q: What three things can change and break an ML system?
a: Code, data and the model. Only code changes are caught by normal DevOps.
analogy: A recipe (code), ingredients (data) and the cook's skill (model).

subject: mlops
q: Why is the ML code only a small part of an ML system?
a: Data collection, features, serving, monitoring and config dwarf the model code and carry most of the risk.
analogy: The model is the engine; MLOps is the rest of the car.

subject: mlops
q: What are Google's MLOps maturity levels 0, 1 and 2?
a: 0 manual notebooks; 1 automated training pipeline with continuous training; 2 CI/CD for the pipeline itself.
analogy: Hand-built release → scripted release → fully automated release train.

subject: mlops
q: What is an ML platform (e.g. Uber Michelangelo)?
a: Shared internal tooling for data, training, registry, serving and monitoring so teams don't rebuild them.
analogy: An internal PaaS, but for models.

subject: mlops
q: What is a baseline and why build it first?
a: The simplest possible predictor, like always the average; a real model must clearly beat it to be worth deploying.
analogy: Checking a new database index beats a full table scan.

subject: mlops
q: What is training-serving skew?
a: Production computes inputs differently from training, so the model sees data it never learned from.
analogy: Testing on Chrome while users run an old Safari.

subject: mlops
q: How do you prevent training-serving skew?
a: One feature function (or feature store) used by both the training pipeline and the serving API.
analogy: One shared library instead of two copy-pasted versions.

subject: mlops
q: What is experiment tracking?
a: Recording every training run's params, data version, metrics and model file.
analogy: Git log plus test results, for training runs.

subject: mlops
q: What is a model registry?
a: Single source of truth for model versions and which one is in Production.
analogy: A container registry with a movable 'production' tag.

subject: mlops
q: How is a model packaged for deployment?
a: Serialise the model (joblib, ONNX, TorchScript) and run the service in a container; mount the model so code and model ship separately.
analogy: Ship the app image; load the config file at start-up.

subject: mlops
q: What is a quality gate in an ML pipeline?
a: Automatic rules a new model must pass before promotion, like CI that must be green.
analogy: Branch protection: no merge until checks pass.

subject: mlops
q: Why compare champion and challenger on the same data?
a: Different eval data makes errors incomparable; a better model can be wrongly rejected, or a worse one accepted.
analogy: Benchmark two servers with the same load test, not different ones.

subject: mlops
q: What does an orchestrator like Airflow or Kubeflow do?
a: Runs the pipeline steps as a DAG on a schedule or trigger, with retries and logs.
analogy: cron plus a dependency graph plus a dashboard.

subject: mlops
q: Batch vs online vs streaming serving?
a: Score a file on a schedule / answer each request live / score events as they flow.
analogy: Nightly report vs API call vs Kafka consumer.

subject: mlops
q: What questions decide how to serve a model?
a: Load, latency, location, hardware, execution mode and where request-time features come from.
analogy: Capacity planning for any service.

subject: mlops
q: Why return the model version with every prediction?
a: So any prediction can be traced to the exact model and training run when debugging or auditing.
analogy: Build number in the response header.

subject: mlops
q: What is data drift?
a: Input distributions change from what the model was trained on.
analogy: Your API suddenly gets traffic from a new country.

subject: mlops
q: What is concept drift?
a: The relationship between inputs and the right answer changes.
analogy: Same order details, but monsoon roads now make it 6 minutes slower.

subject: mlops
q: What is PSI and its thresholds?
a: Population Stability Index: how much a feature's distribution moved; < 0.1 ok, 0.1-0.25 watch, > 0.25 alert.
analogy: A diff score between two histograms.

subject: mlops
q: Why monitor drift if you can monitor accuracy?
a: True outcomes often arrive late (hours or weeks), so input drift is the early warning.
analogy: Smoke detector before the fire report.

subject: mlops
q: What is a shadow deployment?
a: New model runs on real traffic but only logs answers; users see the old model.
analogy: Dark launch of a backend service.

subject: mlops
q: What is a canary release?
a: A small share of users get the new model first; ramp up if metrics hold.
analogy: Rolling out an app update to 10% of users.

subject: mlops
q: Stateless vs stateful retraining?
a: Stateless retrains from scratch on recent data; stateful continues training the existing model on new data only.
analogy: Full rebuild vs incremental build.

subject: mlops
q: What is continuous training (CT)?
a: Retraining automatically on a schedule or a trigger such as a drift alert.
analogy: A CI pipeline that also rebuilds the model.

subject: mlops
q: What is federated learning?
a: Training across many devices where only model updates leave the device, never the raw data.
analogy: Each phone sends a diff, never the files.

subject: mlops
q: Name three model compression techniques.
a: Quantization (lower precision), pruning (remove weights), distillation (small model learns from a big one).
analogy: Minify and compress a JS bundle.
